description: K8s reap hang root cause (warren-c433): after pod-exit terminal, streamWithSignal's finally awaited iterator.return() on the pod-log async generator, which parks forever on an empty queue with no follow EOF — run stuck 'running' indefinitely and the in-pod finalize-intent poll deadlocked (warren only parks intent at reap, reap never ran). Lesson: any 'drain then abort' path over a provider stream needs a hard time bound.
resolution: boundedTeardown races iterator.return() against 5s (DEFAULT_STREAM_TEARDOWN_MS); finalize() parks intent when terminal observed via pod exit; watchdog-reconcile.ts force-finalizes running rows whose pod is terminal past WARREN_RUN_TERMINAL_RECONCILE_GRACE_MS (120s default).

title: Stay on GKE Autopilot; fix SSD quota via boot-disk class, not quota increases
rationale: SSD_TOTAL_GB (500GB us-west1) was 455GB used with only 55GB PVCs — ~400GB is Autopilot node boot disks (100GB pd-balanced each; pd-balanced counts against SSD quota). Quota bumps auto-denied twice (1000, 750; 48h cooldown). DISKS_TOTAL_GB pool is 4TB with 0 used, so a custom ComputeClass with storage.bootDiskType pd-standard decouples scale-up from SSD quota entirely.
